title: Working With Chronically Suicidal People
subtitle: Wisdom from Dr. Vint Blackburn
body_html:
The Frontier Psychiatrists started as a room on the app Clubhouse. Carlene and I started hosting these social audio rooms before they could be recorded, and we had some colleagues join us. I wanted to do one of those rooms on the topic of mass shootings, and I asked a friend who told me, given his role with the government, that he couldn't do it. So he recommended a colleague who he thought would do a great job. That colleague was Dr. Vint Blackburn. Vint is a child and an adult psychiatrist also, and was a teacher before he became a physician. We had a lot in common! Both of us had some other job first, which colored our approach to the work that we did. I was recording engineer, as my readers may remember. Vint became a regular on our weekly shows.

Share

Vint and I shared a passion for working with people who are suicidal. It's really difficult challenge for many, but his levelheaded approach always appealed to me. He's also a great teacher, having been an actual literal teacher previously, just like I had been.

He made the following video recently, and I just had to share with my readers. He talks about working with chronically suicidal people, and uses the metaphor of watching someone drowned in a river. Will jump into them and drag them out first time without hesitation, and maybe the second time, and maybe the third, but everyone gets exhausted at a certain point. What do we do then? Vint Blackburn calls this “on the shores of the river, but not jumping in.”

I couldn't recommend guidance for those helping people with chronic suicidal thoughts or actions more strongly.

Thanks for reading, and watching, today. If you like this, he has a whole YouTube channel, and you should subscribe to it and share with everybody you know.
